drhp.business: Ajwa Fun World and Resort Limited operates a recreation and hospitality destination in the Vadodara / Waghodiya area of Gujarat, combining an amusement park, a water park and resort facilities for family, corporate-outing and event visitors. The promoter, a long-standing real-estate developer, diversified the family's construction interests into the Amusement Park, Water Park and Resort business, and the company has been listed on the BSE since 1994. During FY26 the routed report states the company disposed of a large immovable property and proposed to diversify its business activities.
drhp.end_markets: Domestic leisure visitors in Gujarat, centred on Vadodara / Baroda|Family and weekend entertainment traffic
drhp.expansion: No new capacity addition, project or commissioning timeline is disclosed. Capital activity in FY26 ran the other way: the Company disposed of its immovable property at CTS number NA 62 and land admeasuring 69,973 sq mtrs bearing CTS number NA 63 (P) at Village Rayantal wadi, Taluka Waghodia, District Baroda, stating the sale was to optimise the asset portfolio and meet business and financial requirements, with proceeds to be utilised towards repayment of borrowings, capital expenditure and diversification of business. On the existing estate the stated vector is asset optimisation - focused …

litigation.note: Not court litigation but a live statutory-penalty exposure: the Secretarial Audit Report (Form MR-3, Annexure-III) for FY26 lists outstanding SOP fines levied by the exchange against the company for non-submission and late submission under Regulations 31, 33, 34 and 6(1) of the SEBI LODR Regulations, several still shown as fully outstanding. The same report also flags that independent-director fees were not paid, the required examination was not taken, mandatory policies were not hosted on the website as required under Regulation 46, and that compliance with State entertainment/tourism taxes was not verified.
litigation.where_read: Secretarial Audit Report (Annexure-III, Form MR-3) inside the routed profile bundle

risks.note: The Directors' Report states the Company generated no revenue from operation during the year as it proposed to diversify its business activities - the operating amusement/resort business effectively stopped contributing, leaving the year's result dependent on an exceptional item rather than trading.
risks.risk: No revenue from operations in the year under review

risks.note: The proposed diversification of business activities is stated without naming a target business, an investment plan or a timeline, so there is no disclosed basis on which to judge execution, and the proceeds of the property sale are earmarked for it alongside debt repayment and capex.

The Company sold its immovable property at CTS number NA 62 and land admeasuring 69,973 sq mtrs bearing CTS number NA 63 (P) at Village Rayantal wadi, Taluka Waghodia, District Baroda. The land base underpinning a single-site amusement-park and resort operator is materially reduced by such a sale, and the registered office was itself shifted out of the Ajwa Nimeta Road compound during the year.
risks.risk: Disposal of the principal immovable property

risks.note: A post-year-end material change: the Company has received a request from the Promoters / Promoter Group to reclassify their shares from 'Promoter and Promoter Group' to 'Public', and the reclassification is under process - a structural change in who is accountable for the Company at the same time as the business is being repositioned.
risks.risk: Promoter / Promoter Group seeking reclassification to Public category

risks.note: The board skills matrix rests the Company on the promoter Chairman & Managing Director (promoter of the Ajwa Group, a real-estate developer of some 40 years' standing) and on Mr Rahil Jain, who is a relative of the Chairperson; the other directors are described in generic competency terms, with no disclosed successor or second line.
risks.risk: Key-man and family concentration at the top of the Company

risks.note: Mr Arvind Manubhai Vakil ceased to be an Independent Director on his death on 21 September 2025 and a replacement additional Independent Director was appointed only with effect from 12 January 2026, leaving the Audit, Nomination & Remuneration and Stakeholders' committees short of independent members for most of the year; the Audit Committee is described as comprising Independent Directors while also listing a non-executive director who is a relative of the Chairperson, and one independent director attended only one of the eight board meetings.

As on 31 March 2026, 55.90% of the Company's total paid-up capital was in dematerialised form, leaving a large minority of the capital in physical form - a transferability and liquidity constraint for shareholders.
risks.risk: Low dematerialisation of the share capital

risks.note: Directors did not recommend a dividend for the year under review in order to conserve the financial resources of the Company, so shareholder return depends entirely on the outcome of the pending diversification.
